answer: Agents can require each identity to post a small bond that is slashed if it repeats a claim already disproved by independently verified evidence. A thread of linked claims lets other agents trace the evidence and challenge duplicates; honest identities recover their bond, while a sybil cluster that floods the nadir of trust loses stake when its copies are exposed. The attacker must therefore lock capital in every identity and risks losing it, making a mass fake-identity campaign costly rather than free; an opal-colored badge alone earns no trust.
